overview:
About This Report

This report provides an overview of the team's SSM® Assessment strengths profile and how it may relate to patterns of communication, collaboration, and overall team dynamics at work. It is designed to support self-awareness, reflection, and developmental discussion in team and workshop settings.

The SSM Assessment measures personality — how the team collectively tends to behave — rather than abilities or skills (what you are good at) or interests (what you enjoy doing). It is not intended to provide any clinical diagnosis.

The Assessment is grounded in established personality research and has completed phase one psychometric validation. Report insights should still be interpreted as indicative tendencies rather than definitive predictive measures, and the tool is not intended for hiring, promotion, or related HR decisions.

In this report, your SSM Assessment strengths profile is also conceptually aligned to O*NET Work Styles and Work Activities.

The O*NET Resource Center is a professional workforce research portal providing data, tools, technical documentation, and support. It is widely recognised as a global standard in workplace metrics.

howToReadMatrix:
How to Read This Chart

The Shaw Strengths Matrix (SSM) synthesises four interrelated frameworks into one, providing nuanced insights into individual unique preference rankings.

SSM defines character strengths as "Stable, positive traits expressed in our behaviour that contribute to wellbeing and flourishing." Individual survey responses were scored and ranked using a standardised algorithm. Higher-ranked Strengths are those more readily accessible and guide responses in real-world situations more often.
howToReadAssessmentTable:
How to Read This Chart

The Team Assessment Table ranks the team's averaged presence of the 12 SSM strengths from 1 (strongest) to 12 (least expressed), grouped into Signature, Supporting, Stretch, and Situational categories.
howToReadWorkStyles:
How to Read This Chart

This chart maps the team's 12 ranked SSM strengths to the 12 core O*NET Work Styles.
howToReadWorkActivities:
How to Read This Chart

This chart shows the team's 12 ranked SSM strengths alongside the O*NET Work Activities most strongly aligned with each strength.
howToReadDistribution:
How to Read This Chart

The chart displays the team's strength distribution, with strengths arranged from the highest average expressed strength on the left to the lowest on the right.
Each bar represents a strength and is divided into coloured segments showing how team members ranked it across four categories. Together, the segments total 100% of responses.

• Signature strengths (#1-#3) – core strengths the team consistently demonstrates.
• Supporting strengths (#4-#6) – readily accessible reinforcements of core strengths.
• Stretch strengths (#7-#9) – effective when required but needing extra effort.
• Situational strengths (#10-#12) – used primarily in specific situations.
howToReadChangeAlignment:
How to Read This Chart

This chart relabels the team's 12 ranked SSM Strengths into 12 Strength Responses to change. It ranks which Strength Responses to change are most likely to cluster within a team and become overexpressed under pressure, translating into Resistant Behaviour risks. The Reframing Strength narrative suggests a complementary strength that can balance that risk.

Confidence.risk: Arrogance – inflated self-belief limits openness to input and obscures blind spots
Confidence.reframe: Discernment - to apply critical judgment and identify what is truly relevant

Courage.risk: Recklessness – rapid action without adequate sense-checking, increasing avoidable risk
Courage.reframe: Practicality - to remain grounded and composed, focusing on effective, workable solutions

Curiosity.risk: Scatteredness – diffused focus on numerous priorities weakens execution and follow-through
Curiosity.reframe: Prudence - to exercise caution, constrain scope, and mitigate risk

Discernment.risk: Hypercriticality – excessive focus on flaws reduces perspective and undermines balanced judgment
Discernment.reframe: Fairness - to restore proportionality, context, and balanced perspective

Discipline.risk: Rigidity – inflexible attachment to established methods and status reduces adaptability to change
Discipline.reframe: Objectivity - to assess options independently and generate unbiased recommendations

Empathy.risk: Enmeshment – over-identification with others’ emotions blurs boundaries, undermining judgment
Empathy.reframe: Courage - to maintain focus on self-directed actions even in the face of others’ discomfort due to factors beyond your control

Fairness.risk: Indecisiveness – over-weighting perspectives delays decisions and risks lack of closure
Fairness.reframe: Tenacity - to drive clear, time-bound commitments and persist through obstacles

Foresight.risk: Idealisation – overly optimistic vision lacks grounding in execution and constraints
Foresight.reframe: Discipline - to convert vision into structured, resource-backed plans

Objectivity.risk: Disconnection – over-reliance on logic weakens emotional engagement and reduces others' buy-in
Objectivity.reframe: Empathy - to emotionally connect with others’ lived experience and foster engagement

Practicality.risk: Stubbornness – over-reliance on familiar solutions and reluctance to consider alternatives
Practicality.reframe: Curiosity - to explore alternative solutions and incorporate new information to improve outcomes

Prudence.risk: Avoidance – over-weighting risk delays action and stalls progress
Prudence.reframe: Confidence - to balance risk with opportunity and project self-assured capability

Tenacity.risk: Obsession – narrow goal fixation limits perspective and risks misaligned effort
Tenacity.reframe: Foresight - to refocus on longer-term vision and ensure alignment of current efforts

strengthResponse.Confidence: Confidence - expresses strong self-belief in their ability to support the change successfully.
strengthResponse.Courage: Courage – acts purposefully even in the face of uncertainty and risk, undaunted by unpredictable outcomes.
strengthResponse.Curiosity: Curiosity – rapidly explores multiple new approaches and ideas, prioritising learning and sharing over convergence.
strengthResponse.Discernment: Discernment – highlights concerns that the change design does not fully account for edge cases.
strengthResponse.Discipline: Discipline – expresses concern that change may disrupt the reliable execution of established processes and plans.
strengthResponse.Empathy: Empathy – raises concern about the human impact of role changes or reductions on colleagues’ morale and wellbeing.
strengthResponse.Fairness: Fairness – regards change as an opportunity to strengthen inclusive, equitable alignment of competing stakeholder interests.
strengthResponse.Foresight: Foresight – emphasises the long-term benefits of change, with limited focus on near-term transition costs.
strengthResponse.Objectivity: Objectivity – advocates for continuous, evidence-based change as essential for competitiveness, unclouded by bias toward the status quo.
strengthResponse.Practicality: Practicality – weighs change against real-world constraints, favouring workable solutions that keep the team productive.
strengthResponse.Prudence: Prudence – flags risks that moving too quickly could expose the organisation to financial, legal or reputational loss.
strengthResponse.Tenacity: Tenacity – sustains effort and remains committed to achieving goals despite obstacles created by change.
